observations: A blocky upright figure fills the center against a gray background; its upper section shows an open-mouthed head with pointed ear-like forms, circular eye marks, and dense zigzag lines for teeth.

Broad overlapping strokes of orange, yellow, green, blue, and red run vertically through the torso, while pink looping lines and small knotted marks repeat at regular intervals along the figure's outer edges.
The lower section ends in three flat rectangular foot-shapes, each filled with tight black zigzag lines; a similar zigzag cluster appears at the lower right edge, separate from the main figure.
reading: The figure stands squarely, arms out, feet planted — a posture that reads as confrontational or braced. Bright vertical color bands push through the body while the black outline holds everything in a rigid frame. The repeated pink knot marks along the joints give the structure a wired, assembled feeling, somewhere between toy and threat. The open mouth with its jagged line teeth pulls the mood toward something unsettled.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between nnxyz nnotb #28 — a loose sprawling figure on a flat orange field — and nnxyz nnotb #30, which uses a similar upright jointed structure on teal. The gray background and dense interior color occupy a middle ground between those two.

connections.reason: Both works show an upright jointed figure with arms extended and zigzag foot forms, but #30 uses a clean teal field while #29 layers color bands over gray, making the structural similarity and tonal difference directly visible.
nifty faces #52 shares the gray background, circular cross-marked eye forms, and open-toothed mouth shape, offering a close formal parallel to the head section of #29 from a different owned series.

lookingQuestion: The pink looping knots appear at nearly every joint along the figure's arms and sides — what do they do to your sense of whether this structure is held together or about to come apart?
ambiguities: The separate zigzag cluster at the lower right edge is unclear — it may be a detached limb, a shadow element, or an independent mark unconnected to the main figure.
Title-derived order and recorded creation order align for this work in the owned subset, but gaps exist elsewhere in the nnotb family, so adjacency does not confirm an unbroken sequence.
